title_en: Chinese Academy of Sciences and Chengdu Institute of Organic Chemistry v. Chengdu Zhengda Electrical Machinery Factory — patent infringement dispute
keywords_en: Civil; patent infringement dispute; first instance; intermediate people's court; Sichuan Province; legal person; Patent Law; determination of patent infringement; statute of limitations; comparison of technical features; utility model patent; patent infringement; technology transfer; patent right; guarantee; patent infringement dispute of a large electrical machinery factory
full_text_en:
Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chengdu Organic Chemistry Research Institute v. Chengdu Zhengda Electrical Machinery Factory — Patent Infringement Dispute

Plaintiff: Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chengdu Organic Chemistry Research Institute. Domicile: No. 9, Section 4, Renmin South Road, Chengdu.

Legal Representative: Jiang Yaozhong, Director of the Institute.

Agents ad litem: Zhang Mofang, Staff Member of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chengdu Organic Chemistry Research Institute; Luo Lun, Attorney at Chengdu Guomao Law Firm.

Defendant: Chengdu Zhengda Electrical Machinery Factory. Domicile: No. 4, East Second Road, Chengdu North Railway Station.

Legal Representative: Lai Yi, Factory Director.

Agents ad litem: Lai Yu, Deputy Factory Director of Chengdu Zhengda Electrical Machinery Factory; Zhao Chuanhua, Attorney at Sichuan Sichuang Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chengdu Organic Chemistry Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as the "Research Institute"), filed a lawsuit with the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province against the defendant, Chengdu Zhengda Electrical Machinery Factory (hereinafter referred to as "Zhengda Factory"), regarding a patent infringement dispute.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, Zhengda Factory, produces and sells a "Zhengda brand secondary purifier for ozone and indoor air of photocopiers" (hereinafter referred to as the "secondary purifier"), the main technical features of which fall within the scope of protection of the claims of three utility model patents owned by the plaintiff and licensed for a fee to Chengdu Kecheng Environmental Engineering Technology Development Company (hereinafter referred to as "Kecheng Company"): "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers," "Indoor Air Purifier," and "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan," thereby infringing the plaintiff's patent rights. The plaintiff requests that the court order Zhengda Factory to immediately cease production and sale of the infringing products, compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 150,000 caused by the infringement, publicly apologize to the plaintiff in the *China Patent Gazette*, *Sichuan Daily*, and *Chengdu Evening News* to eliminate the adverse effects, and guarantee that no further infringement will occur.

To support its claims, the plaintiff, the Research Institute, submitted the following evidence:

Evidence 1–3: Certificates of utility model patents, patent specifications, and claims for the three utility model patents granted to the plaintiff by the Patent Office of the People's Republic of China, namely, "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers" (Patent No. 87205109.9), "Indoor Air Purifier" (Patent No. 89213104.7), and "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" (Patent No. 90211733.5), together with receipts for payment of annual patent fees.

Evidence 4 and 6: Product manuals, price lists, and pictures of the "secondary purifier" produced by the defendant, Zhengda Factory.

Evidence 5: The "Consultation Opinion on Patent Infringement Technical Determination" issued by the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office on August 26, 1996, upon entrustment by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, regarding whether the "secondary purifier" falls within the scope of protection of the Research Institute's patent claims.

Evidence 7: A certificate issued by Jinan Tianqiao Zhongnan Modern Office Equipment Co., Ltd. stating that it received an advertisement for the sale of the "secondary purifier" at the end of 1994.

Evidence 8: An invoice from the defendant, Zhengda Factory, for printing 2,000 advertisements for the "secondary purifier" on March 31, 1995.

Evidence 9: Inspection Report No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950780) issued by the Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute on September 1, 1995, for the "secondary purifier."

Evidence 10–18: Certificates from entities such as Sichuan Provincial Electric Power Bureau and EDS Company regarding the purchase or consignment of the "secondary purifier."

Evidence 19: A patent technology transfer agreement signed on March 30, 1990, between the plaintiff, the Research Institute, and Kecheng Company concerning "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers," "Indoor Air Purifier," and "Exhaust Gas Purifier for Type Casting Machines."

Evidence 20: An ordinary license contract signed on July 8, 1990, between the plaintiff, the Research Institute, and Kecheng Company for the implementation of the "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" patent.

Evidence 21: A contract signed on June 30, 1993, between the plaintiff, the Research Institute, and Kecheng Company for the acceptance of technical achievements from a research group for the "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers."

Evidence 22–35: Fourteen transfer checks and accounting vouchers for a total of RMB 986,090.59 paid by Kecheng Company to the plaintiff, the Research Institute, under the headings of technology transfer fees, management fees, remittances, technology use fees, comprehensive technology fees, and technology achievement use fees, between April 4, 1994, and November 20, 1997.

Defendant's Defense: (1) The defendant uses a patented technology entitled "Secondary Purifier for Ozone and Indoor Air of Photocopiers" to produce the "secondary purifier," and the product has passed quality inspection and obtained a recommendation certificate. It is not in the same field as the plaintiff's patents and is not comparable. (2) The impeller used by the defendant was lawfully purchased from Jiuliti Plastics Factory. (3) The plaintiff's utility model patent for "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers" expired on July 17, 1995. (4) The plaintiff knew as early as March 1994 that the defendant was developing the "secondary purifier" but did not file suit until May 1996, which exceeds the statute of limitations. In summary, the defendant has not infringed the plaintiff's three patents.

To support the above claims, the defendant, Zhengda Factory, submitted the following evidence:

Evidence 1: A certificate of utility model patent granted by the Patent Office to Lai Yu on January 28, 1996, for "Secondary Purifier for Ozone and Indoor Air of Photocopiers" (Patent No. ZL94229927.2), and the patent specification and claims.

Evidence 2: Inspection Reports No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950780) and No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (961529) issued by the Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute on September 1, 1995, and October 18, 1996, respectively, after inspecting the "secondary purifier."

Evidence 3: A product recommendation certificate issued by the Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute on October 20, 1996, for the "secondary purifier," and a statement from the defendant.

Evidence 4 and 11: The enterprise standard for the "secondary purifier" formulated by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, and the "secondary purifier" manual.

Evidence 5: A letter of entrustment dated September 19, 1995, from Kecheng Company to Chengdu Jin Niu District Jiuliti Plastics Factory for processing impellers.

Evidence 6: A receipt dated May 29, 1996, issued by Jiuliti Plastics Factory for the purchase of 100 impellers by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, at a price of RMB 300.

Evidence 7: An agreement dated October 22, 1994, between Kecheng Company and the defendant, Zhengda Factory, for the entrustment of the production of an impeller mold; and transfer checks and VAT invoices dated June 16, 1995, and July 18, 1995, for the mold fee paid by Kecheng Company to Zhengda Factory.

Evidence 8: The "Consultation Opinion on Patent Infringement Technical Determination" issued by the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office on August 26, 1996.

Evidence 9: The "Decision on Request for Examination of Invalidation Announcement" issued by the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office on March 14, 1998, for "Indoor Air Purifier" (Patent No. 89213104.7).

Evidence 10: A receipt dated December 16, 1995, issued by Chengdu Jinjiang District Tianbei Printing Factory for the payment by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, for printing 2,000 copies of the "secondary purifier" manual.

During the court investigation, the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court examined the evidence submitted by both parties. The defendant, Zhengda Factory, raised no objection to Evidence 1–6, 8–10, and 16 submitted by the plaintiff, the Research Institute; it raised objections to Evidence 7, 11–15, and 17–35. The Research Institute raised no objection to the evidence submitted by Zhengda Factory except for Evidence 6. Upon trial, the following facts were established:

I. The utility model patent "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers" (Patent No. 87205109.9) owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, had a protection period ending on July 18, 1995. The basic features of Claim 1 of this patent are: It consists of a hood (1), a connecting pipe (2), a purifier housing (3), an exhaust fan (4), an exhaust pipe (5) for the exhaust fan, and a purified exhaust pipe (7), characterized by a purification box (6) containing a catalyst disposed within the purifier housing (3), one side of the purification box being connected to the exhaust pipe (5) of the exhaust fan, and the other side being connected to the purified exhaust pipe (7).

The utility model patent "Indoor Air Purifier" (Patent No. 89213104.7) owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, had a protection period ending on July 31, 1997. The basic features of Claim 1 of this patent are: It consists of a purifier housing (1), an exhaust fan (2) disposed within the housing (1), a connecting pipe (3) connected to the exhaust pipe of the exhaust fan (2), a purified exhaust pipe (5), and a fragrance device (6) disposed at or near the outlet of the purified exhaust pipe (5), characterized by a purification box (4) containing an activated carbon adsorbent disposed within the purifier housing (1), one side of the purification box being in communication with the connecting pipe (3), and the other side being in communication with the purified exhaust pipe (5).

The utility model patent "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" (Patent No. 90211733.5) owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, had a protection period ending on January 12, 1998. The basic features of Claim 1 of this patent are: It has a hub (3) at its center portion that can be connected to the rotating shaft of the centrifugal fan, with fastening screws (4) on the hub (3) for tightening; characterized by one end of the hub (3) being provided with a circular bottom plate (5) perpendicular to the hub (3), having a central circular hole, the periphery of which is sealingly connected to the outer circumference of the hub, on the side of the circular bottom plate (5) facing the hub (3), there are a plurality of arc-shaped blades (2) of identical shape arranged evenly along the peripheral portion, perpendicular to the surface of the circular bottom plate (5), the number of which may be equal to or greater than eight, the concave surfaces of each arc-shaped blade (2) facing the direction of rotation of the motor shaft of the fan, the radius of curvature R of the concave surfaces of the arc-shaped blades (2) being ≥ 6 mm, the angle θ between the chord line connecting the two ends of the concave surface and the extension line from the center of the impeller to the endpoint of the chord line near the center of the impeller being 0° ≤ θ ≤ 60°, the other ends of each arc-shaped blade (2) being connected to an annular plate (1), which is parallel and concentric with the circular bottom plate (5). The low-noise impeller for the centrifugal fan consists of the annular plate (1), the circular bottom plate (5), and the plurality of arc-shaped blades (2) disposed perpendicularly and evenly between the two plates (1, 5), centered around the hub (3).

After obtaining the above three patents, the plaintiff, the Research Institute, licensed them to its subsidiary Kecheng Company for a fee at varying annual rates. From August 16, 1995, to January 12, 1998, Kecheng Company paid a total of RMB 584,521.57 in patent implementation license fees to the Research Institute.

II. The utility model patent "Secondary Purifier for Ozone and Indoor Air of Photocopiers" (Patent No. ZL94229927.2) used by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, for producing the "secondary purifier" was filed on November 29, 1994, and published for announcement on September 6, 1995. The basic features of Claim 1 of this patent are: It consists of a gas collection box (1), a connecting pipe (2) connected to the gas collection box, a purifier housing (3), an air inlet cover wall (4), an exhaust fan housing (5), an exhaust fan wheel (6) connected thereto, an exhaust air duct (7), activated carbon (8) for primary purification of photocopier ozone, an air outlet (9) of the primary purification box for photocopier ozone, an air inlet (10) for secondary purification of ozone and indoor air, fastening screws (11) for the exhaust fan, a purification box (12), an air purification sterilization lamp (13), activated carbon (14) for secondary air filtration, a fragrance device (15), an exhaust outlet (16) for purified air, a double-headed motor (17), an indoor air inlet (18), a photocopier (19), a partition (20) within the purification box, a mesh screen (21) within the purification box, a motor shaft (22), a motor mounting seat (23), and screws (24) for connecting the purification box. The "secondary purifier" includes all components of the patent except for the air purification sterilization lamp (13), the fragrance device (15), and the photocopier (19).

The Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute conducted quality inspections on the "secondary purifier" produced by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, and issued Inspection Reports No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950780) on September 1, 1995, and No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (961529) on October 18, 1995. Both inspection conclusions stated that the product met the standards for the tested items. The inspection report No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950780) indicated that the enterprise standard reference number was B5101001821-1996, and the inspection results were as follows: purified dust emission concentration at 2.73 mg/m³ (dry standard), dust purification efficiency at 59.66%, ozone purification efficiency at 85.42%, and purified ozone emission concentration at 6.39 × 10⁻³ mg/m³ (dry standard).

On August 16, 1995, the defendant, Zhengda Factory, sold one "secondary purifier" to the Sichuan Provincial Electric Power Bureau. On March 2, 1998, it sold one "secondary purifier" to Chengdu Enwei Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

III. On October 22, 1994, Kecheng Company entrusted the defendant, Zhengda Factory, to process an impeller mold, and the parties signed an entrustment agreement. The agreement stated that the impeller was to be used for the photocopier ozone purifier and that the mold was exclusively owned by Kecheng Company. The impeller used by Zhengda Factory in producing the "secondary purifier" is identical to the technical solution set forth in Claim 1 of the utility model patent "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" (Patent No. 90211733.5) owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute.

The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court held:

I. Although the "secondary purifier" produced by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, uses the utility model patent "Secondary Purifier for Ozone and Indoor Air of Photocopiers" granted to Lai Yu, the technical solution used in producing the product is equivalent to the scope of protection of Claim 1 of the two utility model patents "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers" and "Indoor Air Purifier" owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, thus falling within the scope of protection of "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers" and "Indoor Air Purifier" by equivalent means.

II. The impeller used by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, in producing the "secondary purifier" is identical to the technical solution set forth in Claim 1 of the utility model patent "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, thus falling within the scope of protection of "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" by identical means.

III. The utility model patent "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers" owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, expired on July 18, 1995. The defendant, Zhengda Factory, first produced and sold the "secondary purifier" on August 16, 1995. Therefore, the "secondary purifier" does not constitute infringement of the "Ozone Purifier for Photocopiers."

Since the utility model patents "Indoor Air Purifier" and "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute, were effective until July 31, 1997, and January 12, 1998, respectively, the "secondary purifier" produced by the defendant, Zhengda Factory, from August 16, 1995, infringed the Research Institute's utility model patent rights for "Indoor Air Purifier" and "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan."

IV. From August 16, 1995, to January 12, 1998, Kecheng Company paid the plaintiff, the Research Institute, a license fee of RMB 584,521.57 for the above three patents. The Research Institute claimed damages based on the license fee it charged others for implementing its utility model patents, requesting the defendant, Zhengda Factory, to compensate for losses of RMB 150,000. This claim complies with legal provisions and should be upheld.

V. The defendant, Zhengda Factory, argued in its defense that the "secondary purifier" it produced was actually only two sets of photocopier ozone purifiers and had no air purification function. This argument is inconsistent with the conclusions of the inspection reports No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950780) and No. Cheng Zhi Jian (Dian) Zi (961529) issued by the Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute and is therefore not upheld.

VI. The defendant, Zhengda Factory, argued in its defense that the plaintiff, the Research Institute, knew as early as March 1994 that the factory was producing the "secondary purifier" but did not file suit until May 1996, thus exceeding the statute of limitations. Zhengda Factory failed to provide corresponding evidence to support this claim, and therefore it is not upheld.

VII. The defendant, Zhengda Factory, argued in its defense that the impeller it used was lawfully purchased and therefore should not constitute infringement of the utility model patent "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" owned by the plaintiff, the Research Institute. When Zhengda Factory processed the impeller mold for Kecheng Company on October 22, 1994, Kecheng Company had already declared in the entrustment agreement that the impeller was to be used for the photocopier ozone purifier and that the ownership of the impeller belonged to Kecheng Company. Therefore, Zhengda Factory knew that the impeller was a specialized product for the photocopier ozone purifier and that its technical solution was completely identical to the utility model patent "Low-Noise Impeller for a Centrifugal Fan" owned by the Research Institute. Accordingly, Zhengda Factory's claim of non-infringement is not upheld.

Article 59 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The scope of protection of a patent for invention or utility model shall be determined by the content of its claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the claims." Paragraph 1 of Article 60 provides: "Where any party, without authorization of the patentee, exploits the patent, thereby infringing the patent rights of the patentee, the patentee or any interested party may request the patent administrative authority to handle the matter, or may directly institute legal proceedings in a people's court." Accordingly, the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on June 29, 1999:

I. The defendant, Zhengda Factory, shall compensate the plaintiff, the Research Institute, for losses of RMB 150,000 caused by its infringement.

II. The defendant, Zhengda Factory, shall publicly apologize to the plaintiff, the Research Institute, in the *China Patent Gazette*, *Sichuan Daily*, and *Chengdu Evening News* to eliminate the adverse effects.

The court acceptance fee for this case is RMB 4,550, and other costs are RMB 1,865, to be borne by the defendant, Zhengda Factory.

Zhengda Factory, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court, contending: I. The "secondary purifier" produced by the appellant is actually two sets of "photocopier ozone purifiers," as pointed out by the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office in the "Consultation Opinion on Patent Infringement Technical Determination." The photocopier ozone purifier and the "Indoor Air Purifier" have different scopes of use, different technical themes and purposes of invention, and do not belong to the same technical field. This is the conclusion reached by the Patent Reexamination Board in its Decision No. 977 on the Request for Examination of Invalidation Announcement regarding the differences between the photocopier ozone purifier and the "Indoor Air Purifier." The appellant's "secondary purifier" is also used to purify toner dust from photocopiers, does not belong to the same technical field as the "Indoor Air Purifier," and therefore does not infringe the patent rights for the "Indoor Air Purifier." II. The impeller technology used by the appellant in manufacturing the fan was lawfully obtained from Meixian County, Shaanxi Province in 1993. The Patent Law provides that exploitation of a patent with the authorization of the patentee or the manufacture of an identical product or use of an identical method before the patent application date, or where necessary preparations for such manufacture or use have already been made, shall not be deemed infringement. Therefore, the appellant's lawful use of such an impeller to manufacture the fan does not constitute infringement. The appellant requests that the court of second instance vacate the original judgment and render a fair decision anew.

Appellee: Chengdu Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences (hereinafter "CIOC") argues: First, the "Patent Infringement Technical Judgment Advisory Opinion" issued by the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office of the People's Republic of China mentions that the appellant's infringing product may constitute two sets of "ozone purifiers for photocopiers," but it does not exclude the possibility that the second set of "ozone purifier for photocopiers" can simultaneously serve as an "air purifier," nor does it conclude that the appellant's infringing product is definitively two sets of "ozone purifiers for photocopiers." Additionally, Decision No. 977 on the Request for Examination of Invalidation Announcement is a response made by the Patent Reexamination Board at the appellant's request, addressing whether the appellee's "indoor air purifier" is novel compared to the appellee's "ozone purifier for photocopiers." The evidence submitted by the appellant to the Patent Reexamination Board was the appellee's "ozone purifier for photocopiers," not the appellant's "secondary purifier." Therefore, Decision No. 977 relates only to the appellee's "ozone purifier for photocopiers" and does not prove that the appellant's "secondary purifier" presents the same issue. Second, the appellant claims that it manufactured and sold products involving the patent for "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan" prior to the appellee's patent application date, but the invoices it provided do not substantiate this assertion, nor is there other evidence to prove it. In summary, the facts that the appellant infringed the appellee's utility model patents for "indoor air purifier" and "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan" are clear. The first-instance judgment correctly applied the law and should be affirmed.

Sichuan High People's Court finds upon trial:

On October 24, 1990, the Patent Office of the People's Republic of China granted the appellee CIOC the utility model patent for "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan," with a patent application date of January 12, 1990. The amended text of Claim 1 of the patent reads as follows: A low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan, comprising: a bushing (3) at its center for connection to the rotating shaft of the centrifugal fan motor; a fixing screw (4) on the bushing (3) for fixation; a circular bottom plate (5) provided at one end of the bushing (3), perpendicular to the bushing (3), having a central circular hole whose periphery is sealingly connected to the outer circumference of the bushing; on the face of the circular bottom plate (5) facing the bushing (3), along its peripheral portion, there are evenly arranged 24 arc-shaped blades (2) of identical shape, perpendicular to the plate surface of the circular bottom plate (5); the concave surface of each arc-shaped blade (2) faces the rotational direction of the motor shaft; the other end of each arc-shaped blade (2) is connected to an annular plate (1), which is parallel and concentric with the circular bottom plate (5); characterized in that the radius of curvature R of the concave surface of the arc-shaped blades (2) is 10-14 mm, the arc length is 20-24 mm, the thickness is 0.5-1 mm, the height is 26-30 mm, and the angle θ between the chord line connecting the two ends of the concave surface and the extension line from the center of the impeller to the endpoint of said chord line near the impeller center satisfies 30° ≤ θ ≤ 45°.

On July 7, 1992, Zhang Mofang, representative of the appellee CIOC, and Xie Qinghua, representative of Chengdu P.O. Box 125, signed the "Fan Contract between Chengdu P.O. Box 125 and the Environmental Protection Company of Chengdu Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences." The contract stipulated that the fan technology was patented technology provided by Kecheng Company, that the supplier must not disseminate or disclose the relevant technology provided by the demander, and must not transfer or sell it to third parties, etc. The contract bore the economic contract seal of Kecheng Company and the seal of China Electronic Systems Engineering Third Construction Company.

From January 1993 to August 1994, Kecheng Company purchased more than 300 medium and small-sized fans made of metal materials from the appellant Zhengda Factory.

On October 22, 1994, in the "Agreement on Entrusted Manufacturing of Impeller Mold" signed by the appellant Zhengda Factory as Party B and Kecheng Company as Party A, the following content appeared: This impeller is used for an ozone purifier for photocopiers; the mold is to be made based on physical samples and relevant patent materials; the mold entrusted by Party A to Party B for manufacturing shall be the exclusive property of Party A, and Party B shall not transfer it to third parties or use this mold to produce products for third parties. On September 29, 1995, Kecheng Company provided this mold to Jinliudi Plastic Factory in Jinniu District, Chengdu, entrusting it with processing plastic impellers. Starting from August 1995, Zhengda Factory began purchasing plastic impellers from Jinliudi Plastic Factory to produce "secondary purifiers."

The instruction manual for the "secondary purifier" printed by the appellant Zhengda Factory stated: This unit improves the photocopier purification device and adds an indoor purification device, etc. On September 1, 1995, the Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute, based on GB4706.1-92 "Safety and General Requirements for Household and Similar Electrical Appliances," conducted a quality inspection on the "secondary purifier" produced by the appellant Zhengda Factory and issued Inspection Report No. Chengzhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950708). On October 18, 1996, the Institute, based on Q/ZD001-1996 "Enterprise Standard for Photocopier Ozone and Indoor Air Secondary Purifier," conducted another quality inspection on the "secondary purifier" and issued Inspection Report No. Chengzhi Jian (Dian) Zi (961529). The main items inspected in both inspections included: marking, insulation resistance, electrical strength, etc. The inspection conclusions were that the products met the standard requirements for the inspected items. Additionally, in the Product Inspection Notice No. (96) 245, the inspection results for the "secondary purifier" were: dust emission concentration after purification: 2.73 mg/m³ (standard dry); dust purification efficiency: 59.66%; ozone purification efficiency: 85.42%; ozone emission concentration after purification: 6.93×10⁻³ mg/m³ (standard dry).

On May 30, 1996, the appellee CIOC filed a lawsuit on the grounds that the "secondary purifier" produced and sold by the appellant Zhengda Factory infringed its patent rights.

On August 19, 1996, the Sichuan Patent Administration Office entrusted the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office of the People's Republic of China to determine whether the appellant Zhengda Factory's "secondary purifier" (Model JHQ-2-A) fell within the protection scope of the appellee CIOC's utility model patents for "ozone purifier for photocopiers" and "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan." The materials provided included: the utility model patent application specification for "ozone purifier for photocopiers"; the utility model patent application specification for "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan"; the patent specification for "indoor air purifier"; the instruction manual for the "secondary purifier"; and one physical sample of the "secondary purifier" bearing the label "Zhengda Electrical Appliances; Photocopier Ozone and Indoor Air Secondary Purifier; Model: JHQ-2-A; Rated Voltage: AC 220V; Rated Frequency: 50Hz; Rated Input Power: 60W; ZHENGDA brand," etc. Based on this, the Patent Reexamination Board issued the "Patent Infringement Technical Judgment Advisory Opinion," concluding as follows: 1. The ZHENGDA brand "secondary purifier" bearing the label "Zhengda Electrical Appliances" and Model JHQ-2-A falls within the protection scope of Claim 1 of the utility model patent for "ozone purifier for photocopiers" in an equivalent manner; 2. The impeller installed in the "secondary purifier" falls within the protection scope of Claim 1 of the utility model patent for "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan" in an identical manner.

On August 26, 1996, the appellant Zhengda Factory, on the grounds that the appellee CIOC's utility model patent for "ozone purifier for photocopiers" and the utility model patent for "indoor air purifier" both have a purifier housing, an exhaust fan, etc., with the differences being the scope of purification and the provision of a fragrance dispenser at or near the purification exhaust pipe, and that compared to the "indoor air purifier" lacks creativity, requested the Patent Reexamination Board to declare the utility model patent for "indoor air purifier" invalid. In its "Decision on the Request for Examination of Invalidation Announcement," the Patent Reexamination Board held that the technical subject matter of the "indoor air purifier" utility model patent is an indoor air purifier, falling under International Classification A61L9/00, while the utility model patent technology named "ozone purifier for photocopiers" purifies ozone generated by photocopiers or duplicators, falling under Class B01D53/2; the two do not belong to the same class, and their technical subject matters differ. Moreover, the former has the distinguishing feature of a fragrance dispenser, the provision of which has the substantive characteristic of filling the room with fragrant purified air. Therefore, the Board decided to maintain the validity of the utility model patent for "indoor air purifier."

In June 1996, the appellant Zhengda Factory's enterprise standard for the "secondary purifier," filed with the Chengdu Technical Supervision Bureau, stated: Used for purifying ozone, organic waste gases, and dust discharged from photocopiers. Performance indicators: When the ozone waste gas discharge volume from the photocopier is 60-100 m³/h, the ozone concentration after purification using Model A shall not exceed 0.1 mg/m³, etc.

It is further found that: The appellant Zhengda Factory is a collectively-owned enterprise registered with the Administration for Industry and Commerce on January 1, 1993. The legal representative at the time of registration was Xie Qinghua.

On July 2, 1999, the Patent Office issued the "Decision on the Review of the Request for Revocation of the Patent Right," revoking the utility model patent for "photocopier ozone and indoor air secondary purifier" granted to Lai Yu on January 28, 1996, on the grounds of lack of creativity.

In addition, the court of second instance affirmed the other facts found in the first instance.

Sichuan High People's Court holds:

The utility model patents of the appellee CIOC for "ozone purifier for photocopiers," "indoor air purifier," and "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan" expired on July 18, 1995, July 31, 1997, and January 12, 1998, respectively. Patent rights within their validity periods shall be protected by law.

Regarding the relationship between the "secondary purifier" produced and sold by the appellant Zhengda Factory and the utility model patent for "ozone purifier for photocopiers" of the appellee CIOC, the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office, in the "Patent Infringement Technical Judgment Advisory Opinion," has already determined that the ZHENGDA brand "secondary purifier" product produced by Zhengda Factory, bearing the label "Zhengda Electrical Appliances" and Model JHQ-2-A, falls within the protection scope of Claim 1 of the utility model patent for "ozone purifier for photocopiers" in an equivalent manner. Since the utility model patent for "ozone purifier for photocopiers" of CIOC expired on July 18, 1995, the technical solution for the ozone purifier for photocopiers became publicly known technology thereafter. Therefore, the "secondary purifiers" produced by Zhengda Factory after August 1995 do not constitute infringement of that utility model patent.

Regarding the issue of whether the "secondary purifier" produced and sold by the appellant Zhengda Factory infringes the utility model patent for "indoor air purifier" of the appellee CIOC. CIOC argues that, based on the Product Inspection Notice of the Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute, Inspection Reports No. Chengzhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950780) and No. (961529), and the description in the "secondary purifier" product manual, the product has dual functions of photocopier ozone purification and indoor air purification, and therefore infringes the utility model patent for "indoor air purifier." To determine the actual performance of a product, the primary consideration should be its structure and actual effects. According to the "Enterprise Standard for Photocopier Ozone and Indoor Air Secondary Purifier" filed by Zhengda Factory with the Chengdu Technical Supervision Bureau, the "secondary purifier" is used to purify ozone, organic waste gases, and dust discharged from photocopiers, with the ozone concentration parameter after purification of the photocopier waste gas discharge as the performance indicator. From the Product Inspection Notice of the Chengdu Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute, it can be seen that the Institute only inspected the degree of photocopier ozone purification. Furthermore, the two inspection reports of the Institute, No. Chengzhi Jian (Dian) Zi (950780) and No. Chengzhi Jian (Dian) Zi (961529), also only inspected safety aspects of the "secondary purifier" such as marking and protection against electric shock, and did not address whether the product had air purification performance. Upon disassembly and examination of the "secondary purifier," the product did not contain the "fragrance dispenser," which is a substantive feature of CIOC's "indoor air purifier" utility model patent. Therefore, Zhengda Factory's "secondary purifier" essentially only has the function of treating photocopier ozone. Zhengda Factory's claim that its product is only used for purifying photocopier ozone and ink dust, unrelated to indoor air purification, is well-founded and should be supported. CIOC's claim that the "secondary purifier" has dual functions of photocopier ozone purification and indoor air purification is not supported by corresponding facts and is not upheld. Therefore, although part of the technical solution of the "secondary purifier" is equivalent to that of the "indoor air purifier," it does not constitute infringement of the utility model patent for "indoor air purifier."

Regarding whether the "secondary purifier" infringes the utility model patent for "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan." After the amendment of the claims of the appellee CIOC's patent for "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan," although the scope of protection narrowed, during the cross-examination of the physical evidence of the impeller, both parties acknowledged that: during the period from 1993 to 1994, the impellers in the metal fans produced and sold by the appellant Zhengda Factory to Kecheng Company had the same technical parameters as the plastic impellers used after August 1995. Both parties also acknowledged that the technical parameters of the plastic impellers used by Zhengda Factory in the "secondary purifier" were substantially consistent with the technical parameters recorded in the amended claim 1 of CIOC's impeller patent. Therefore, the impeller technology used in Zhengda Factory's products falls within the protection scope of Claim 1 of CIOC's patent for "a low-noise impeller for a centrifugal fan," constituting infringement of that patent. The Patent Reexamination Board's "Patent Infringement Technical Judgment Advisory Opinion" also made this determination. Zhengda Factory appeals, claiming that its technology for producing metal impellers was lawfully obtained from Mei County, Shaanxi Province in 1993. Since CIOC's impeller patent application date was January 12, 1990, Zhengda Factory's defense of prior use right against CIOC's patent right is untenable. Zhengda Factory also argues that CIOC knew that Zhengda Factory had begun producing and selling impellers identical to the patented technology as early as 1993 but only filed suit in May 1996, claiming that CIOC's lawsuit exceeded the statutory limitation period. Zhengda Factory cannot provide evidence proving that CIOC "knew earlier," so this claim by Zhengda Factory is not supported.

The facts found in the first-instance judgment are basically clear, and the trial procedure is lawful, but the application of law is partially improper. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Sichuan High People's Court hereby renders judgment on April 5, 2000, as follows:

1. The first item of the first-instance civil judgment is reversed;

2. The second item of the first-instance civil judgment is affirmed;

3. The appellant Zhengda Factory shall pay RMB 50,000 in damages for the losses caused to the appellee CIOC due to its infringing acts.
